n20368068825.s:
Consider the following statements about the layers of the Sun from the centre outward:
1. The core is the innermost layer.
2. The photosphere lies below the convective zone.
3. The corona is the outermost of the major layers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n20368068825.x: From the centre outward the order is core, radiative zone, convective zone, photosphere, chromosphere and corona, so the photosphere lies above, not below, the convective zone.

n539e5b8432d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the evolution of the early Earth's interior?
o: Materials separated according to their density
Heavy iron sank to form the core
The sinking of iron to the centre is called degassing
n539e5b8432d.x: The sinking of heavy iron to the core and the rise of lighter material to form the crust is called differentiation, not degassing.

ngeneral-geography-1-76.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the tail of a comet?
o: It points away from the Sun
The solar wind helps push it
ngeneral-geography-1-76.x: Radiation pressure and the solar wind push a comet's tail away from the Sun, so it never points towards the Sun.

nfaf4968f394.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the SMILE mission?
o: It is a joint ESA-China mission
It will image the solar wind striking Earth's magnetic shield
It will use X-ray and ultraviolet observations together
It will image in gamma-ray and infrared radiation
nfaf4968f394.x: SMILE will image the solar wind meeting Earth's magnetic shield in X-ray and ultraviolet together, not gamma-ray and infrared.

ngeneral-geography-1-13.s: The weight of an object on the Earth's surface is maximum at the:
ngeneral-geography-1-13.x: Rotation and the equatorial bulge reduce effective gravity at the Equator, so weight is least there and greatest at the poles.

ncf52f2623b1.s: How many parallels of latitude are conventionally drawn on the globe at 1° interval?
ncf52f2623b1.x: There are 89 parallels in each hemisphere plus the Equator, making 179 (the poles are points); there are 360 meridians.

nc141ac3da7c.s: Which of the following cities lies farthest south?
nc141ac3da7c.x: From north to south the order is Srinagar, Bhopal, Visakhapatnam and Chennai, so Chennai is farthest south.

n2a8839ea633.s: The northernmost point of India is:
n2a8839ea633.x: Indira Col in the Karakoram is India's northern extreme; Indira Point is the southernmost, Kibithu the easternmost and Guhar Moti the westernmost point.

ngeneral-geography-2-28.s:
Consider the following statements about the Coriolis effect:
1. It affects cyclones.
2. It is caused by the Earth's revolution around the Sun.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
ngeneral-geography-2-28.x: The Coriolis effect shapes cyclones, but it comes from the Earth's rotation, not its revolution.

n593be1b14f1.s: People do not feel the Earth's rotation mainly because:
o: The Sun's gravity cancels the rotational motion
The Earth's magnetic field absorbs the motion
The Earth's rotation is confined to the polar regions
The atmosphere and objects on Earth move along with it at a nearly uniform speed
n593be1b14f1.x: The Earth's motion is nearly uniform, and the atmosphere and everything on it move along with it, so the motion is not felt.

new.s: The study of the origin, evolution and structure of the universe is called:
new.x: Cosmology is the study of the origin, evolution and structure of the universe.

new.s: One parsec is equal to about:
new.x: A parsec, the largest of the common distance units, equals about 3.26 light years.

new.s: One light year is a distance of about:
new.x: A light year, the distance light travels in a year, is about 9.461 × 10¹² km (~9.46 trillion km).

new.s: Which of the following is the correct order of distance units in increasing size?
new.x: The astronomical unit is the smallest and the parsec (3.26 light years) the largest; a light year measures distance, not time.

new.s: Hydrogen makes up about what share of the Sun's composition?
new.x: The Sun is about 74% hydrogen and about 24% helium.

new.s: The Nebular hypothesis of the origin of the solar system was first proposed by:
new.x: Immanuel Kant proposed the Nebular hypothesis in 1755; Laplace revised it in 1796.

new.s: The Planetesimal hypothesis (1904) is associated with:
new.x: Chamberlin and Moulton put forward the Planetesimal hypothesis in 1904.

new.s: The Tidal hypothesis of the origin of the Earth was given by:
new.x: The Tidal hypothesis is credited to James Jeans and Harold Jeffreys.

new.s: In which year did Georges Lemaitre propose the Big Bang (expanding universe) idea?
new.x: Lemaitre proposed the Big Bang in 1927; Hubble showed the expansion of the universe through red-shift only in 1929.

new.s: The Nova hypothesis of the origin of the solar system is associated with:
new.x: Hoyle and Lyttleton proposed the Nova hypothesis.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (theory – proponent) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Steady State – Hoyle, Bondi and Gold
new.x: The Big Bang was proposed by Georges Lemaitre (1927); Hubble only showed the expansion of the universe (1929).

new.s: The four large moons of Jupiter were first seen by Galileo in:
new.x: Galileo discovered the four Galilean moons of Jupiter (Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto) in 1610.

new.s: Pluto was discovered in 1930 by:
new.x: Clyde Tombaugh discovered Pluto in 1930; Herschel found Uranus and Galle first saw Neptune.

new.s: S. Chandrasekhar presented his black-hole theory paper to the Royal Astronomical Society, London, in:
new.x: Chandrasekhar presented the paper on 11 January 1935.

new.s: Which ancient Indian astronomer stated that the Earth rotates on its axis and explained eclipses?
new.x: Aryabhata (476–550 CE) held that the Earth rotates on its axis and explained eclipses.

new.s: A pulsar is a spinning:
new.x: A pulsar is a spinning neutron star formed from a collapsed massive star.

new.s: A low or medium mass star such as the Sun finally ends its life as a:
new.x: Low and medium mass stars pass through red giant and planetary nebula stages to end as white dwarfs.

new.s: In the life cycle of a star, which stage comes immediately after the nebula?
new.x: A star develops from nebula to protostar and then to the main sequence.

new.s: In the magnitude scale of stars, a lower magnitude number means the star is:
new.x: Magnitude is logarithmic and a lower number means a brighter star.

new.s: Which colour of star has the lowest surface temperature?
new.x: Stars run from blue (hottest) through white, yellow and orange to red (coolest).

new.s: Brittle Star is a:
new.x: Brittle Star is an echinoderm, an animal, not a space object.

new.s: The Sun accounts for about what share of the solar system's mass?
new.x: The Sun holds about 99.8% of the mass of the solar system.

new.s: The temperature of the Sun's core is about:
new.x: Fusion of hydrogen into helium takes place in the core at about 15 million °C.

new.s: Which layer of the Sun is seen during a total solar eclipse and has a temperature of over 1 million °C?
new.x: The corona, the outermost layer, is seen during a total eclipse and is hotter than 1 million °C.

new.s: The reddish lower atmosphere of the Sun, seen during eclipses, is the:
new.x: The chromosphere is the Sun's reddish lower atmosphere, visible at eclipses.

new.s: Coronal mass ejections from the Sun usually reach the Earth in about:
new.x: CMEs travel at 250–3,000 km/s and reach the Earth in about 1–3 days.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about sunspots?
o: They are cooler, dark magnetic patches
They follow a cycle of about 11 years
They are hotter and brighter than the photosphere
new.x: Sunspots are cooler, dark magnetic patches on the photosphere, so they are not hotter or brighter than it.

new.s: Solar flares are bursts of energy produced by:
new.x: Solar flares are bursts released by magnetic reconnection on the Sun.

new.s: Which two planets have retrograde rotation?
new.x: Venus and Uranus rotate in the direction opposite to most planets.

new.s: Which planet rotates fastest on its axis?
new.x: Jupiter, the largest and heaviest planet, also has the fastest spin.

new.s: Which planet has the coldest average temperature (about −200 °C)?
new.x: Neptune has the coldest average temperature; Uranus has the lowest single recorded temperature (about −224 °C).

new.s: Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet'?
new.x: Mars is called the Red Planet.

new.s: Saturn and Jupiter are classed as:
new.x: Jupiter and Saturn are gas giants; Uranus and Neptune are ice giants.

new.s: A day on Mars lasts about:
new.x: Mars's day of 24 h 37 min and axial tilt of 25°12' are close to the Earth's (23 h 56 min; 23°30').

new.s: At its closest, Venus comes within about what distance of the Earth?
new.x: Venus, the planet nearest to the Earth, comes within about 41.4 million km; Mars comes within about 78.4 million km.

new.s: Which is the largest moon of the solar system, bigger even than Mercury?
new.x: Jupiter's Ganymede is the largest moon in the solar system; Titan, Saturn's largest, comes after it.

new.s: Which moon of Jupiter has an ocean under its icy crust?
new.x: Europa, a moon of Jupiter, has an ocean beneath its icy crust.

new.s: After Titan, the second largest moon of Saturn is:
new.x: Titan (5,150 km) is Saturn's largest moon and Rhea its second largest.

new.s: The methane lakes on Titan are about how deep?
new.x: Titan's lakes of liquid methane are about 100 m deep.

new.s: After the moons added in 2026, how many moons does Saturn have?
new.x: Saturn had 274 moons in March 2025 and reached 285 after 11 more were added in 2026; Jupiter has 101.

new.s: Styx and Kerberos are moons of:
new.x: Pluto's five moons are Charon, Styx, Nix, Kerberos and Hydra.

new.s: In the evolution of the early Earth, the first hydrogen-helium atmosphere was lost mainly through the:
new.x: The early hydrogen-helium atmosphere was stripped away by the solar wind before degassing built a new one.

new.s: The Earth's hydrosphere formed mainly when:
o: Degassed water vapour condensed and fell as rain
new.x: Water vapour released by degassing condensed and fell as rain, filling the oceans.

new.s: Degassing from the Earth's interior released mainly:
o: Water vapour, nitrogen and carbon dioxide
new.x: Degassing released water vapour, nitrogen and carbon dioxide to the early atmosphere.

new.s: Compared with an average full Moon, a micromoon appears about:
new.x: At apogee the full Moon is a micromoon, about 6–7% smaller and 10–14% dimmer.

new.s: Higher tides occur when the Moon is at:
new.x: At perigee the Moon is closest to the Earth, giving a supermoon and higher tides.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Perigee – Earth closest to the Sun
Aphelion – Moon farthest from the Earth
Perihelion – Earth closest to the Sun
Apogee – Earth farthest from the Sun
new.x: Terms ending in -helion refer to the Sun (Earth's orbit) and those in -gee to the Earth (the Moon's orbit); perihelion is the Earth's closest point to the Sun.

new.s: The Earth's aphelion falls during which season of the Northern Hemisphere?
new.x: Aphelion (~4 July) falls in the northern summer, showing that seasons come from the tilt, not distance.

new.s: The gravity of the Moon is about what fraction of the Earth's?
new.x: The Moon's gravity is about one-sixth of the Earth's, so an object's weight there falls to 1/6.

new.s: During the Apollo 11 mission, which astronaut stayed in lunar orbit?
new.x: Armstrong and Aldrin walked on the Moon on 20 July 1969 while Collins orbited it.

new.s: Short-period comets come mainly from the:
new.x: The Kuiper Belt (30–50 AU, beyond Neptune) supplies short-period comets; the Oort Cloud supplies long-period ones.

new.s: The largest body in the asteroid belt is:
new.x: Ceres, about 1,000 km across, is the largest body in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.

new.s: A meteor is commonly known as a:
new.x: A meteor is a shooting star; a meteorite is a body that reaches the ground.

new.s: Compared with comets, asteroids generally have orbits that are:
new.x: Asteroids follow less eccentric orbits, while comets move in highly elliptical orbits.

new.s: The Shoemaker-Levy 9 comet crashed into which planet in July 1994?
new.x: Shoemaker-Levy 9, found in March 1993, hit Jupiter on 16–22 July 1994.

new.s: The Hale-Bopp comet has a period of about:
new.x: Hale-Bopp is a long-period comet with a period of about 2,534 years; Halley's period is about 76 years.

new.s: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet at the IAU General Assembly held in:
new.x: The IAU's 26th General Assembly (14–25 August 2006) adopted the new planet definition.

new.s: The discovery of which body triggered the reclassification of Pluto?
new.x: The discovery of Eris led the IAU to define a planet and reclassify Pluto in 2006.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about dwarf planets?
o: Ceres lies in the asteroid belt
Haumea and Makemake lie in the Kuiper belt
Eris is a moon of Jupiter
new.x: Eris is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, not a moon of Jupiter.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the IAU (2006) definition of a planet:
1. A planet must orbit the Sun.
2. A planet must be nearly round.
3. A planet must have at least one natural satellite.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: A planet must orbit the Sun, be nearly round and clear its orbit; having a satellite is not a condition (Mercury and Venus have none).

new.s: NASA's DART mission made a kinetic impact on the asteroid:
new.x: DART struck Dimorphos as a test of planetary defence.

new.s: OSIRIS-REx, renamed OSIRIS-APEX, is headed for the asteroid:
new.x: After returning Bennu samples in 2023, OSIRIS-REx was renamed OSIRIS-APEX to study Apophis in 2029.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (mission – target) is correctly matched?
new.x: ESA's Hera surveys Didymos-Dimorphos after DART; Hayabusa2 sampled Ryugu, OSIRIS-REx sampled Bennu and DART hit Dimorphos.

new.s: Aditya-L1 orbits the Sun–Earth L1 point at about what distance from the Earth?
new.x: Aditya-L1 is in a halo orbit around L1, about 1.5 million km from the Earth.

new.s: How many Lagrange points does a two-body system such as the Sun and Earth have?
new.x: There are five Lagrange points; L4 and L5 are stable and L1–L3 unstable.

new.s: Mangalyaan was launched in November 2013 aboard:
new.x: Mangalyaan was launched on PSLV-C25 and entered Mars orbit on 24 September 2014.

new.s: The VELC payload of Aditya-L1 made the first spectroscopy of coronal mass ejections in:
new.x: VELC made the first visible-light spectroscopy of CMEs, not X-ray.

new.s: SDSC-SHAR, Sriharikota, completed its 100th launch on:
new.x: SDSC-SHAR in Andhra Pradesh made its 100th launch on 29 January 2025.

new.s: The Phoenix Mars Lander, which found ice, landed on Mars in 2008 near the planet's:
new.x: Phoenix landed on 25 May 2008 at Mars's North Pole and found ice.

new.s: The Earth's shape, flattened at the poles and bulging at the Equator, is called an:
new.x: The Earth is an oblate spheroid, flattened at the poles and bulging at the Equator.

new.s: The point on the Earth's surface nearest to its centre lies at the:
new.x: Because of polar flattening, the poles (the Arctic Ocean floor near the North Pole) are nearest the centre.

new.s: The polar diameter of the Earth is about:
new.x: The polar diameter is about 12,714 km, about 43 km less than the equatorial diameter of 12,756 km.

new.s: By about how much is the Earth's polar diameter shorter than its equatorial diameter?
new.x: The polar diameter (12,714 km) is about 43 km less than the equatorial (12,756 km).

new.s: The equatorial circumference of the Earth is about:
new.x: The Earth's circumference at the Equator is about 40,075 km.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a valid latitude?
new.x: Latitudes range from 0° to 90° north or south, so 95°N cannot exist.

new.s: Lines of latitude run in which direction?
new.x: Latitudes (parallels) run east–west, parallel to the Equator; meridians run north–south.

new.s: One degree of latitude represents a distance of about:
new.x: One degree of latitude is about 111 km everywhere.

new.s: The antipode of the point 30°N, 60°E is:
new.x: The antipode of (x°N, y°E) is (x°S, (180 − y)°W), so 30°N 60°E becomes 30°S 120°W.

new.s: Which of the following countries lies on the Tropic of Cancer?
new.x: Niger lies on the Tropic of Cancer, not on the Prime Meridian.

new.s: The Tropic of Capricorn passes through:
new.x: The Tropic of Capricorn crosses Chile, Brazil, South Africa and Australia.

new.s: Which of the following Indian states is NOT crossed by the Tropic of Cancer?
new.x: The Tropic of Cancer crosses eight states, including Jharkhand, Tripura and Chhattisgarh, but not Odisha.

new.s: Which of the following countries is NOT crossed by the Arctic Circle?
new.x: Iceland lies just south of the Arctic Circle, which crosses Norway, Sweden, Finland, Russia and Canada.

new.s: The Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn are how many degrees apart?
new.x: Each Tropic lies at 23.5° from the Equator, so they are 47° apart.

new.s: On the December solstice, the noon Sun's altitude at the Tropic of Cancer is:
new.x: The Sun is overhead at Capricorn, 47° away, so its noon altitude at Cancer is 90° − 47° = 43°.

new.s: Who first used latitude and longitude?
new.x: Ptolemy first used latitude and longitude; Hipparchus divided the circle into 360°.

new.s: The first Greek world map is credited to:
new.x: Anaximander drew the first Greek world map.

new.s: The UNGA resolution of 2026 proposed replacing the Mercator projection with the:
new.x: The non-binding UNGA resolution (September 2026) proposed the Equal Earth projection in place of Mercator.

new.s: The northern limit of Andhra Pradesh's latitude extent is:
new.x: Andhra Pradesh extends from 12°41'N to 19°07'N, not to 22°N.

new.s: The longitudinal extent of Andhra Pradesh is:
new.x: Andhra Pradesh lies between 77°E and 84°40'E.

new.s: In area, Andhra Pradesh ranks among Indian states as:
new.x: Andhra Pradesh, with 1,62,970 sq km (~4.96% of India), is the 7th largest state.

new.s: The east–west extent of India is about:
new.x: India stretches about 2,933 km east–west and 3,214 km north–south.

new.s: Which of the following cities lies farthest north?
new.x: From north to south the order is Visakhapatnam, Hyderabad, Chennai and Kanyakumari.

new.s: The angular speed of the Earth's rotation is:
new.x: The Earth turns 360° in 24 hours, i.e. 15° per hour or 1° every 4 minutes.

new.s: The linear speed of the Earth's rotation at the Equator is about:
new.x: Rotation speed is about 1,670 km/h at the Equator and zero at the poles.

new.s: Seen from above the North Pole, the Earth rotates:
new.x: The Earth spins west to east, which appears counter-clockwise from above the North Pole.

new.s: The solar day is longer than the sidereal day by about:
new.x: The solar day is about 4 minutes longer because the Earth also moves along its orbit while rotating.

new.s: The main cause of the shift in the Earth's rotational axis is:
o: Mass redistribution such as ice melt and groundwater loss
new.x: Axis shift comes mainly from mass redistribution (ice melt, groundwater loss); solar flares only disturb the upper atmosphere.

new.s: In which year did Foucault demonstrate the Earth's rotation with a pendulum in Paris?
new.x: Foucault's pendulum experiment was performed in Paris in 1851.

new.s: Aryabhata explained the daily rising and setting of the Sun in his work:
new.x: Aryabhata first proposed the Earth's rotation and explained the Sun's daily rise and set in the Aryasiddhanta.

new.s: The circle of illumination is also known as the:
new.x: The circle of illumination, or terminator, is also called the grey line or twilight zone.

new.s: Which country is known as the 'Land of the Midnight Sun'?
new.x: Norway, beyond the Arctic Circle, is called the Land of the Midnight Sun.

new.s: The unequal lengths of day and night through the year are caused by:
o: Tilt of the axis and revolution
new.x: Day and night come from rotation, but their unequal lengths come from the tilt combined with revolution.

new.s: Twilight lasts longest at high latitudes because there the Sun:
o: Rises and sets along an oblique path
new.x: At high latitudes the Sun's oblique path makes twilight long, even weeks near the poles; at the Equator it rises almost vertically.

new.s: The rule that moving air is deflected to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere is called:
new.x: Ferrel's law describes deflection to the right in the NH and to the left in the SH.

new.s: Tropical cyclones rarely form within how many degrees of the Equator?
new.x: Coriolis force is too weak near the Equator, so cyclones rarely form within 5° of it.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Coriolis force:
1. It increases with latitude.
2. It increases with wind speed.
3. It is maximum at the Equator.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Coriolis force (2Ωv sin latitude) grows with latitude and wind speed; it is zero at the Equator and maximum at the poles.

new.s: The equatorial bulge and polar flattening of the Earth are due mainly to the:
new.x: Centrifugal force, maximum at the Equator and zero at the poles, causes the bulge and flattening.

new.s: Spring tides occur when the Sun, the Earth and the Moon are:
new.x: Spring tides occur when the Sun, Earth and Moon are aligned, at new and full moon.

new.s: Successive high tides at a place occur about how far apart?
new.x: There are two high tides a day, about 12 h 25 min apart.

new.s: The mean orbital speed of the Earth around the Sun is about:
new.x: The Earth revolves round the Sun at a mean speed of about 29.78 km/s.

new.s: In 2026, the Earth reached aphelion on:
new.x: In 2026 perihelion fell on 3 January and aphelion on 6 July.

new.s: The shape of the Earth's orbit around the Sun is:
new.x: The Earth's orbit is slightly elliptical, so the Earth–Sun distance is not constant.

new.s: The Sun is overhead at the Equator on:
new.x: At the equinoxes, 21 March and 23 September, the Sun is overhead at the Equator.

new.s: A century year is a leap year only if it is divisible by:
new.x: A century year is a leap year only if divisible by 400, so 2000 was a leap year and 1900 was not.
